Most of the claim holds in src/sqllens/profiles.py. Lines 138-152: OSError, invalid JSON and a non-dict top level each call _flag_corrupt, which sets a 'Warning:' load_error, logs it and returns with no profiles. Nothing deletes the file. Lines 180-189: a bad-name entry sets _invalid_profile_names, and load_error carries only the count. Lines 204-209: _save raises when that flag is set, and upsert and delete both go through _save. Lines 190-202: when all names are valid, load_error names every skipped entry. The claim breaks at lines 165-167. An entry whose body is not a JSON object (e.g. {"a": "str"}) is appended to `skipped` with no logger call. Only the ValidationError branch (lines 170-178) logs a per-entry line. The doc says every skipped entry is 'logged on its own line' and that bad-body entries are 'named only in their per-entry log lines' when a bad name is also present. For a non-object body alongside a bad name, the entry is never named anywhere: load_error gives only the count and there is no per-entry log. So the doc is wrong for that input.
